speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a neonate presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth; tell me, were there any complications during your pregnancy, delivery, or the first few days of life?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of chorioamnionitis, low Apgar scores, and a history of prematurity makes infection and hypoxic-ischemic injury high on the differential; have you noticed any fever, poor feeding, or changes in color? REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, Blood_Culture, Glucose.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The tense fontanelle, sluggish pupils, and conjugate eye movements are highly concerning for increased intracranial pressure and meningeal irritation; given the history of chorioamnionitis, we must proceed immediately with the CSF analysis. Once the pending lumbar puncture results return, we will have the definitive data to distinguish between sepsis and meningitis. Are there any other specific symptoms, such as a rash or respiratory distress, you have observed?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Meningitis
